subject: System Design
title: Measuring Load
description: A quick, practical guide to Measuring Load.

hook.text: Before you can scale, you need to know what you're scaling. What metric defines your load?

buildup.text: Load parameters vary: requests per second, concurrent connections, database reads, or cache hit ratio.

discovery.text: Twitter's key load parameter is fan-out: each tweet must reach thousands of followers' timelines.

twist.text: Optimizing the wrong metric wastes effort. A system bottlenecked on writes won't benefit from read caching.

climax.text: Identify your load parameter first, then design your scaling strategy around it.

punchline.text: Measure the right thing before scaling anything.

quiz.question: What is a load parameter?
options: A metric that defines the system's primary load, like requests per second
